title: llama.cpp Hits 1.0 With a Stable API Promise for Local AI
dek: The open-source local AI engine now follows semantic versioning.
caption:
If you've ever run a chatbot on your laptop, this one's for you 💻

llama.cpp, the open-source engine behind a huge share of local AI apps, just hit version 1.0 alongside its ggml library. The headline isn't a flashy feature. It's a promise: breaking changes to the public API now only come with a major version bump, following semantic versioning across all ggml-org projects.

The release also packs FP8 key-value caches, new text, vision and text-to-speech models, security hardening for llama-server and a redesigned web UI. NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM and Intel are helping with testing, and installs are easier via Homebrew, Winget, conda-forge and Docker.

At AI Parabellum, we see this as the moment a hobby tool becomes real infrastructure. Stable foundations mean faster support for new open-weight models in the apps you already use.

Trust is the real feature in llama.cpp 1.0. The local AI engine now guarantees that only major versions will break its API, so developers can update without fear.

Running llama-server on a network? Update soon for the new SSRF, CORS and DNS rebinding fixes 🔒
